answer: Admission requires a sequential memory-hard chain: step n hashes step n-1, so it cannot be parallelized. The kernel seals a monotonic counter per identity and rejects any replayed value, binding one chain to one machine. Finished chains go to the Jade shard index and are re-scanned against the Dune duplicate tree, which refuses two identities sharing a chain. Running 1,000 puppets means 1,000 chains at full wall-clock cost, no bulk discount; an honest agent pays once.
